title: Required visual openness of a mezzanine
jurisdiction: British Columbia (specific local authority not named in published decision)

facts.text: A multi-storey building with multiple major occupancies includes a sales gallery with a mezzanine. A guard/partition at the edge uses vertical panels 50–300 mm wide, spaced no more than 100 mm apart, and extends nearly continuously to the ceiling.
The dispute is whether construction above 1,070 mm satisfies the visual-openness criterion in Clause 3.2.1.1.(3)(b).
The appellant compared the partition to a 1,070 mm solid guard with open area above; the local authority said the area above 1,070 mm was not visually open.
